nodes.content: For t=1,...,T, adversary chooses y_t in [0,1] secretly, player chooses x_t in [0,1], then y_t is revealed. Example 2.32 replaces squared loss by absolute loss.

nodes.content: dom f={x:f(x)<+infinity}.
Convexity means convex epigraph.

anchor.locator: Theorem 2.7, sole display and Rockafellar citation

nodes.content: For convex f:R^d -> (-infinity,+infinity], x in int dom f and f differentiable at x, f(y)>=f(x)+<gradient f(x),y-x> for all y. Cited Rockafellar (1970), Theorem 25.1 and Corollary 25.1.1, external proof not reproduced.

anchor.locator: Theorem 2.8 statement and two proof paragraphs

nodes.content: On nonempty convex V, for f convex and differentiable on an open set containing V and x* in V, x* minimizes f iff <gradient f(x*),y-x*>>=0 for all y in V. Sufficiency uses 2.7; necessity uses a feasible line segment and negative directional derivative contradiction.
x_1 in nonempty closed convex V, positive eta_t. Predict x_t, pay convex differentiable loss, take g_t=gradient loss_t(x_t), update x_(t+1)=Pi_V(x_t-eta_t g_t).
Pi_V(x)=argmin_(y in V)||x-y||_2 is asserted to be the unique Euclidean projection; ||Pi_V(x)-y||_2<=||x-y||_2 for y in nonempty closed convex V.

anchor.locator: Proposition 2.11 proof, continues PDF25 top display

nodes.content: Equality of norm and half-squared-norm argmin, application of Theorem 2.8 gives <Pi_V(x)-x,y-Pi_V(x)>>=0; squared-distance expansion and nonnegative terms give contraction toward each feasible y.

anchor.locator: Lemma 2.12 statement and its full proof display

nodes.content: eta_t(loss_t(x_t)-loss_t(u))<=eta_t<g_t,x_t-u><=||x_t-u||^2/2-||x_(t+1)-u||^2/2+eta_t^2||g_t||^2/2. Uses projection contraction, squared-norm expansion and gradient support.

anchor.locator: Theorem 2.13 first display; proof PDF26 first display

nodes.content: For diameter D and 0<eta_(t+1)<=eta_t, R_T(u)<=D^2/(2 eta_T)+sum eta_t||g_t||^2/2-||x_(T+1)-u||^2/(2 eta_T). Divide one-step by eta_t, sum, rearrange weighted distances, bound distances by D using nonnegative inverse-rate differences, telescope inverse-rate differences.

anchor.locator: Theorem 2.13 Moreover display; proof PDF26 second display

nodes.content: For constant eta>0, R_T(u)<=||u-x_1||^2/(2 eta)+(eta/2)sum||g_t||^2-||x_(T+1)-u||^2/(2 eta). Constant coefficients telescope exactly.
The terminal-distance term is nonpositive and may be discarded for a weaker bound, though retained by the source theorem.

anchor.locator: First two displays and However paragraph

nodes.content: Formal minimization using comparator distance and future gradient energy is unavailable online: future gradients depend on eta, comparator is unknown, adversary can react to the learning rate.

anchor.locator: For the moment paragraph; eta-star display; numbered equation (2.1)

nodes.content: Assume ||g_t||_2<=L and bounded diameter D. Minimize D^2/(2 eta)+eta L^2 T/2 to obtain eta*=D/(L sqrt(T)) and bound D L sqrt(T). Tuning is for fixed number of iterations (PDF26 final paragraph).
Pi_[0,1](z)=min(max(z,0),1). Statement supplied without its scalar proof.
Proper means nowhere -infinity and finite somewhere.

anchor.locator: Definition 2.20 and sole display; PDF29 opening paragraph

nodes.content: For proper f, g is a subgradient at x iff f(y)>=f(x)+<g,y-x> for all y. Partial f(x) is the set of all such g; subdifferentiable iff nonempty.
For f(x)=|x|, partial f(x)={1} if x>0, [-1,1] if x=0, {-1} if x<0. No proof displayed.
For proper f and h(x)=f(Ax+b), A^T partial f(Ax+b) is a subset of partial h(x). Proof substitutes affine arguments into the subgradient support inequality. Inclusion only, not equality.

anchor.locator: Section 2.2.2 first paragraph and its support display

nodes.content: Theorem 2.13 analysis uses loss_t(x_t)-loss_t(u)<=<g_t,x_t-u>; this holds for any subgradient, so the regret bounds transfer with differentiability replaced by subdifferentiability.
For nonempty closed convex V, loss subdifferentiable on V, eta_t>0, g_t in partial loss_t(x_t), projected update, the complete two-inequality one-step bound of 2.12 holds for every u in V.

anchor.locator: Algorithm 2.2 Require and lines 1-6; following paragraph

nodes.content: Start x_1 in nonempty closed convex V, eta_1,...,eta_T>0; output x_t, pay subdifferentiable loss, choose g_t in partial loss_t(x_t), update with Euclidean projection. The prose identifies line 4 as the change from Algorithm 2.1.
Reuse Chapter 1 guessing game with loss_t(x)=|x-y_t|, requiring subgradients because the losses are nondifferentiable.
partial loss_t(x)={1} for x>y_t, [-1,1] for x=y_t, {-1} for x<y_t. The source allows the entire interval at equality, with no specified tie selection.
Running OSD with the optimal learning rate gives a regret of O(sqrt(T)) as T tends to infinity. This sentence gives no explicit eta, finite-T constant, or comparator formula.
Existence and uniqueness of the Euclidean argmin for a nonempty closed convex set are asserted, not proved in the direct source region.
Scalar clipping characterization is stated without a proof.
Complete absolute-value subdifferential characterization is given without proving support or the reverse exclusion.

nodes.content: Translation of the complete absolute subdifferential is not proved. Theorem 2.28 supplies an inclusion, not the reverse inclusion needed for equality.
No written calculation discharges V=[0,1] closed/convex/nonempty, D=1, |g_t|<=1, eta=1/sqrt(T)>0 for T>=1, or substitutes these into the transferred bound.

anchor.locator: A Winning Strategy, first paragraph, beginning Can we win the number guessing game? and ending the adversary.

nodes.content: The guessing game can also be won when the adversary chooses its number after observing the player choice. The source imposes no restriction on how the adversary decides the numbers and explicitly allows adversarial choices. Thus the initial secret-before-prediction ordering on PDF13 is not a restriction on the later guessing-game guarantee. The player still receives y_t only after outputting x_t.

derived_instantiation.objects: For each fixed integer horizon T>=1, y_1,...,y_T in [0,1], allowing y_t to be chosen after observing current x_t, any x_1 in [0,1], any causal allowed choice g_t in partial |.-y_t|(x_t) after y_t is revealed, and any u in [0,1].
derived_instantiation.update: x_(t+1)=min(max(x_t-eta*g_t,0),1), eta=1/sqrt(T). A tie may use any g_t in [-1,1].

discharges.L: All three source case sets are contained in [-1,1], so |g_t|<=1, including ties.
discharges.loss_domain: loss_t is the finite ambient function R -> R, not an extended-real constrained loss.
discharges.rate: T>=1 implies eta>0; eta is constant during that horizon, with T known for this specialization.
discharges.iterates: Initial feasibility and projection preserve x_t in [0,1].
discharges.feedback: The player outputs x_t before learning y_t. The adversary may choose y_t after observing x_t (PDF15, A Winning Strategy first paragraph); once y_t is revealed, the case subgradient is available. The support and distance proof is pathwise and requires no independence or pre-output choice restriction.
discharges.terminal: -(x_(T+1)-u)^2/(2 eta)<=0 is discarded only in the weaker upper bound.

derived_instantiation.upper_asymptotic: The displayed finite inequality implies an eventual one-sided upper bound R_T(u)<=C sqrt(T) with C=1. The source writes O(sqrt(T)); it does not supply a two-sided |R_T(u)| bound. Do not silently equate these contracts.
derived_instantiation.best_fixed: Continuity of sum_t |u-y_t| on compact [0,1] gives a minimizing comparator; applying the uniform bound there gives best-fixed regret <=sqrt(T). This standard bridge is derived and not displayed in Example 2.32.
boundaries: No assertion that R_T(u) is nonnegative.
No fixed horizon-independent anytime sequence is specified by this tuning.
No iid, martingale, confidence or probability requirement.
No scalar tie convention or sign(0) definition specified.
No exact finite constant or explicit learning rate is printed in Example 2.32 itself.
